notes: Supplied primary title/DOI verified. PDF pages 9 and 10 rendered and visually inspected. Original side is an unassigned placeholder. No row mapping by audit ID, order, original-page sequence, or matching numeric values. Methods p. 2782 gives recruitment N = 273 and allocation n = 48 intervention, n = 56 no-intervention peer, n = 169 no-intervention non-peer; Table 1 p. 2785 repeats these group counts. These are not explicit final analytic counts for a specified critical model. Procedure p. 2783 reports one student withdrew from school mid-intervention. No analytic N sum performed and no N inferred from dfs. Printed F/t metrics retained as candidates without conversion. Canonical backslashes in p expressions represent <, verified visually in supplied PDF. Candidate tests on p. 2786/PDF 9: Knowledge condition F(2, 238) = 17.12, p < .001; time F(2, 476) = 45.35, p < .001; interaction F(4, 476) = 28.65, p < .001. Attitude time F(1.79, 425.81) = 16.90, p < .001; condition F(2, 238) = 3.10, p = .05; interaction F(3.58, 425.81) = 1.51, p = .21. The same page also reports post/follow-up between-condition knowledge tests, within-condition repeated-measures tests and paired time contrasts; none is uniquely designated. Knowledge intervention pre/post t(46) = -9.71, p < .001, d = 1.78; pre/follow-up t(45) = -9.53, p < .001, d = 1.82. Both rows with p. 9 have identical replication descriptions/locators and cannot be distinguished. Authors describe positive knowledge and attitude changes, marginal behavioural-intention improvement without maintenance, and variable spill-over. These are candidate narrative judgments; no unique row-specific verdict assigned.
